Sabatini & Kaufman (2024) on DANDI:000070: trial reading (b)¶

This notebook is reproduce_sabatini_2024.ipynb with two parameters changed in its first code cell: READING = "b" (successful trials with a delay above 400 ms, reading (b) of the claims file's shared method) and FULL_SEEDS = False (each claim's own seed only). Every analysis and every claim cell is the same. It shows the results under the trial reading the main notebook does not adopt; the conclusions, and the outcomes, are in the main notebook, which cites these numbers where the two readings differ.

Dataset: DANDI:000070, version 0.260528.0919, streamed. Paper: doi:10.1038/s41467-024-51308-7.

In [1]:
import os
for _v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ[_v] = "1"  # many small fits, some in parallel worker processes (protocol)
import time
import zlib
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
import ldr

# Trial reading of the claims file's shared method that the analyses use: "a", all successful trials
# of the 72 conditions (adopted: the Methods describe the task with a 0-1000 ms delay and name no
# exclusion), or "b", successful trials with a delay above 400 ms. The companion notebook
# reproduce_sabatini_2024_trials_b.ipynb is this notebook with READING = "b" and FULL_SEEDS = False.
READING = "b"
# Run the four extra seeds of each claim (protocol); the companion notebook runs the claim's own seed only.
FULL_SEEDS = False
# Leave out the units found in "Unit checks" whose spike train is not one stable unit's (the paper used
# "single-units and stable multi-units"). The companion notebook reproduce_sabatini_2024_stable_units.ipynb
# is this notebook with EXCLUDE_UNSTABLE = True.
EXCLUDE_UNSTABLE = False
T_START = time.time()
DATASETS = [("J", "M1"), ("J", "PMd"), ("N", "M1"), ("N", "PMd")]
NAME = {d: f"{d[1]}-{d[0]}" for d in DATASETS}


def seed(claim):
    """The claim's seed (protocol): crc32 of '<paper key>/<claim id>'."""
    return zlib.crc32(f"sabatini-2024/{claim}".encode())


def seeds5(claim):
    return [seed(claim) + i for i in ((0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000) if FULL_SEEDS else (0,))]


print("dandiset", ldr.DANDISET, "version", ldr.VERSION, "| trial reading", READING, "| five seeds", FULL_SEEDS,
      "| unstable units left out", EXCLUDE_UNSTABLE)

dandiset 000070 version 0.260528.0919 | trial reading b | five seeds False | unstable units left out False

Loading¶

Each session is streamed once. Spike times are binned at 1 ms from 500 ms before to 1000 ms after movement onset, smoothed with a Gaussian of 20 ms s.d. and sampled every 10 ms from -350 to +850 ms (Methods, Subjects, behavior and data pre-processing; claims, shared method). The time-shuffled copies for tbf-shuffle-control are made at load time under that claim's five seeds, a copy shuffled over the span of the paper's code (the analysis window) under the claim's own seed, and the warped copies for fig3i at the same time.

In [2]:
SESS = {}
for m in ("J", "N"):
    t0 = time.time()
    SESS[m] = ldr.load_session(m, shuffle_seeds=seeds5("tbf-shuffle-control"),
                               shuffle_window_seeds=[seed("tbf-shuffle-control")])
    print(m, "loaded in", round(time.time() - t0), "s; trials kept (successful, 72 conditions):",
          len(SESS[m]["trials"]["maze_condition"]))

Conditions and trial readings¶

The claims file gives two readings for the 72 conditions (drop maze conditions that are a multiple of 3; drop the 3-target versions, whose distractors repeat a curved maze) and two for trials: (a) all successful trials, (b) successful trials with a delay above 400 ms. Both trial counts are within 10% of the paper's (1469 and 2014), (a) above them and (b) below. The analyses use the reading set in READING above. This notebook adopts reading (a): the Methods describe the task with "a brief delay (0–1000 ms)" and name no exclusion of short delays (Methods, Subjects, behavior and data pre-processing), and the analyses are of peri-movement activity aligned to movement onset. This is an assumption, recorded. The companion notebook reproduce_sabatini_2024_trials_b.ipynb runs every analysis under reading (b).

Clock check¶

Spikes and the trial table must share a clock. For each recording segment, the condition of a trial is decoded from spike counts in -100 to +300 ms around movement onset (nearest centroid, leave one trial out; chance 1/72). As a contrast, the same decoder is run with each trial's activity paired with the condition of the previous trial in the segment.

In [5]:
def clock_check(m, units=None):
    S = SESS[m]
    tr = S["trials"]
    cond = CT[m]["cond"]
    gi = (ldr.GRID_MS >= -100) & (ldr.GRID_MS <= 300)
    F = S["R"][:, :, gi].mean(2)
    if units is not None:
        F = F[:, units]
    out = []
    for sg in np.unique(tr["segment"]):
        ii = np.where((tr["segment"] == sg) & MASK[m])[0]
        res = []
        for lab in (cond[ii], np.r_[cond[ii][-1], cond[ii][:-1]]):
            X = F[ii]
            hits = 0
            for q in range(len(ii)):
                o = np.ones(len(ii), bool)
                o[q] = False
                cs = np.unique(lab[o])
                cen = np.array([X[o & (lab == c)].mean(0) for c in cs])
                hits += cs[np.argmin(((cen - X[q]) ** 2).sum(1))] == lab[q]
            res.append(hits / len(ii))
        # trained on the other segments, tested on this one
        oth = np.where((tr["segment"] != sg) & MASK[m])[0]
        cross = np.nan
        if len(oth):
            cs = np.unique(cond[oth])
            cen = np.array([F[oth][cond[oth] == c].mean(0) for c in cs])
            pred = cs[np.argmin(((F[ii][:, None, :] - cen[None]) ** 2).sum(2), 1)]
            cross = (pred == cond[ii]).mean()
        out.append((sg, len(ii), res[0], res[1], cross))
    return out


for m in ("J", "N"):
    for sg, n, acc, acc_sh, cross in clock_check(m):
        print(f"{m} segment {sg}: {n} trials, condition decoded {acc:.3f} (labels of the previous trial {acc_sh:.3f}; "
              f"trained on the other segments {cross:.3f}; chance {1/72:.3f})")

Unit checks¶

The paper used "single-units and stable multi-units" (Methods, Subjects, behavior and data pre-processing). Three units of the dandiset are not one stable unit's. In the Jenkins file one unit's spike train holds two sorted runs one after the other; the cell prints each run's size and span, the spike times they share, intervals under 1 ms, how many of each run's times are found exactly in another unit's train, and any unit whose train ends just before a run begins. In the Nitschke file, the cell prints each segment's per-trial summed rate, and, per unit, the largest mean rate over blocks of 50 successive trials divided by the median block mean (ldr.block_rate_ratio); a unit above 5 is unstable (a threshold chosen here; the cell prints the ratios, so that the range of thresholds giving the same units can be read off). The clock check is repeated without the unstable units. The main analyses keep every unit, as before; the companion notebook reproduce_sabatini_2024_stable_units.ipynb leaves out the units the cell lists (DROP).

RUNS = {}
for m in ("J", "N"):
    S = SESS[m]
    if S["info"]["n_hand_segments"] == 1:
        for un in np.where(S["info"]["unit_jumps"] > 0)[0]:
            RUNS[(m, int(un))] = ldr.spike_run_report(m, un)
for (m, un), rep in RUNS.items():
    print(f"{m} unit {un} ({SESS[m]['area'][un]}), one recording segment: runs (spikes, first s, last s)",
          [(n, round(a, 1), round(b, 1)) for n, a, b in rep["runs"]])
    print(f"   spike times found in both runs: {rep['shared']}; intervals under 1 ms: merged train {rep['isi_below_1ms_merged']:.4f}, "
          f"each run {[round(x, 4) for x in rep['isi_below_1ms_runs']]}")
    print("   largest fraction of each run's times found exactly in another unit's train (fraction, unit):",
          [(round(f, 3), int(o)) for f, o in rep["most_shared_with_other_unit"]])
    for o, n, a, b, (fr, o3) in rep["ends_before_a_run"]:
        print(f"   unit {o} ({SESS[m]['area'][o]}): {n} spikes from {a:.1f} to {b:.1f} s, ending "
              f"{(min(r[1] for r in rep['runs'] if r[1] > b) - b) * 1000:.0f} ms before a run of unit {un} starts; "
              f"largest fraction of its times found exactly in another unit's train {fr:.3f} (unit {o3})")

gi_ = (ldr.GRID_MS >= -100) & (ldr.GRID_MS <= 300)
for m in ("J", "N"):
    tr = SESS[m]["trials"]
    tot = SESS[m]["R"][:, :, gi_].mean(2).sum(1)
    for sg in np.unique(tr["segment"]):
        ii = (tr["segment"] == sg) & MASK[m]
        print(f"{m} segment {sg}: {int(ii.sum())} trials; per-trial rate summed over units, -100 to +300 ms (spikes/s), "
              f"percentiles 0/5/50/95/100: {np.round(np.percentile(tot[ii], [0, 5, 50, 95, 100])).astype(int).tolist()}")

RATIO = {m: ldr.block_rate_ratio(SESS[m]["R"]) for m in ("J", "N")}
UNSTABLE = {}
for m in ("J", "N"):
    o = np.argsort(-RATIO[m])[:4]
    UNSTABLE[m] = np.where(RATIO[m] > 5)[0]
    print(f"{m}: block rate ratio, largest four (unit: ratio)", {int(u): round(float(RATIO[m][u]), 2) for u in o},
          "| median over units", round(float(np.median(RATIO[m])), 2), "| above 5:", UNSTABLE[m].tolist())
    for un in UNSTABLE[m]:
        tr = SESS[m]["trials"]
        fr = SESS[m]["R"][:, un].mean(1)
        for sg in np.unique(tr["segment"]):
            ii = (tr["segment"] == sg) & MASK[m]
            print(f"   unit {un} ({SESS[m]['area'][un]}) segment {sg}: mean rate {fr[ii].mean():.1f} spikes/s, "
                  f"median {np.median(fr[ii]):.1f}, trials above 100 spikes/s {int((fr[ii] > 100).sum())} of {int(ii.sum())}")
        st = SESS[m]["trials"]["start_time"]
        hi = (fr > 100) & MASK[m]
        if hi.any():
            print(f"   trials above 100 spikes/s start from {st[hi].min():.0f} to {st[hi].max():.0f} s (segment clock)")

DROP = {m: sorted(set(UNSTABLE[m].tolist()) | {un for (mm, un) in RUNS if mm == m}) for m in ("J", "N")}
KEEP = {m: np.ones(len(SESS[m]["area"]), bool) for m in ("J", "N")}
for m in ("J", "N"):
    if EXCLUDE_UNSTABLE:
        KEEP[m][DROP[m]] = False
    print(f"{m}: units not one stable unit's {DROP[m]} ({[str(SESS[m]['area'][u]) for u in DROP[m]]}); "
          f"left out in this run: {EXCLUDE_UNSTABLE}")
for m in ("N",):
    keep_u = ~np.isin(np.arange(len(SESS[m]["area"])), UNSTABLE[m])
    for sg, n, acc, acc_sh, cross in clock_check(m, keep_u):
        print(f"{m} segment {sg} without the unstable units: condition decoded {acc:.3f} (labels of the previous trial "
              f"{acc_sh:.3f}; trained on the other segments {cross:.3f})")

Basis functions per dataset¶

For each dataset, condition-averaged rates are formed from the trials of the reading in READING, and the number of temporal basis functions is cross-validated (Methods, Cross-validating the number of temporal basis functions; claims, shared method: k = 1 to 20, two halves of the trials, 100 folds, an even k raised by one). The basis is fitted on -150 to +850 ms (Methods, De-mixing temporal basis functions) and de-mixed. The cross-validation is repeated under the five seeds of fig3g-basis-frequencies.

In [7]:
D = {}
for ds in DATASETS:
    m, area = ds
    S = SESS[m]
    u = (S["area"] == area) & KEEP[m]
    R = S["R"][:, u]
    cond = CT[m]["cond"]
    X = ldr.cond_average(R, cond, 72, MASK[m])
    D[ds] = dict(R=R, X=X, Xw=X[..., ldr.FIT0:], cond=cond, u=u)

def cv_job(args):
    ds, sd = args
    return ldr.cv_tbf_k(D[ds]["R"], D[ds]["cond"], 72, np.random.default_rng(sd), mask=MASK[ds[0]])


_jobs = [(ds, sd) for ds in DATASETS for sd in seeds5("fig3g-basis-frequencies")]
_cv = dict(zip(_jobs, ldr.pmap(cv_job, _jobs)))
CV = {ds: _cv[(ds, seed("fig3g-basis-frequencies"))] for ds in DATASETS}
for ds in DATASETS:
    ks = [int(np.argmax(_cv[(ds, sd)].mean(0)) + 1) for sd in seeds5("fig3g-basis-frequencies")]
    k = ks[0] + (ks[0] % 2 == 0)
    D[ds]["k_cv"] = ks[0]
    D[ds]["k_seeds"] = ks
    # de-mix; drop the last basis function while more than one real (unpaired) mode remains
    # (Methods: 'discarded the last basis function if it was unpaired')
    while True:
        B, L = ldr.tbf(D[ds]["Xw"], k)
        Bd, Ld, lam, grp, fr = ldr.demix(B, L)
        if (grp == -1).sum() <= 1 or k == 1:
            break
        k -= 1
    D[ds].update(k=k, B=Bd, L=Ld, lam=lam, grp=grp, freq=fr, Braw=B, Lraw=L)
    print(NAME[ds], f"({int(D[ds]['u'].sum())} units)", "held-out VE by k:", np.round(CV[ds].mean(0)[:12], 3))
    print("   best k under five seeds", ks, "-> k used", k, "| frequencies (Hz)", np.round(fr, 2),
          "| |eigenvalue|", np.round(np.abs(lam), 3))

Single-condition LDSs: fig2c-condition-lds-variance¶

Activity on each single condition was low-dimensional and approximated by an LDS of 5 to 9 dimensions, which explained 71 to 93% of the population variance.

Dimensionality by cross-validation over two trial partitions, 100 repeats, odd k from 1 to 21 (the code's set; claims), one k per dataset. The Methods' even split is the main reading and the code's 3/4 to 1/4 split a variant.

In [9]:
KS = list(range(1, 22, 2))


def dim_job(args):
    ds, sd, frac, folds = args
    cv = ldr.cv_condition_dim(D[ds]["R"], D[ds]["cond"], 72, np.random.default_rng(sd), KS, folds=folds, mask=MASK[ds[0]], frac=frac)
    return cv.mean((0, 1))


_jobs = [(ds, seed("fig2c-condition-lds-variance"), fr, 100) for ds in DATASETS for fr in (0.5, 0.75)]
_jobs += [(ds, sd, 0.5, 100) for ds in DATASETS for sd in seeds5("fig2c-condition-lds-variance")[1:]]
DIMCV = dict(zip(_jobs, ldr.pmap(dim_job, _jobs)))
for ds in DATASETS:
    cvm = DIMCV[(ds, seed("fig2c-condition-lds-variance"), 0.5, 100)]
    res = {"even split": KS[int(np.argmax(cvm))],
           "3/4 split": KS[int(np.argmax(DIMCV[(ds, seed("fig2c-condition-lds-variance"), 0.75, 100)]))]}
    kd = res["even split"]
    sims, lams = [], []
    for c in range(72):
        Xc = D[ds]["Xw"][c]
        Xs, lam = ldr.rrr_lds(Xc, kd)
        sims.append(ldr.pop_ve(Xc, Xs))
        lams.append(lam)
    D[ds]["lds_k"] = kd
    D[ds]["lds_ve"] = np.array(sims)
    D[ds]["lds_lam"] = lams
    kv = res["3/4 split"]
    ve_v = np.array([ldr.pop_ve(D[ds]["Xw"][c], ldr.rrr_lds(D[ds]["Xw"][c], kv)[0]) for c in range(72)])
    D[ds]["lds_ve_var"] = ve_v
    print(f"{NAME[ds]}: held-out VE by k {dict(zip(KS, np.round(cvm, 3)))}")
    print(f"   chosen k {kd} (even split) | {kv} (3/4 split) ; LDS VE mean {np.mean(sims):.3f} s.d. {np.std(sims):.3f} "
          f"range {np.min(sims):.3f}-{np.max(sims):.3f} | at k={kv}: mean {ve_v.mean():.3f}")
# seed sensitivity of the chosen k
for ds in DATASETS:
    ks = [KS[int(np.argmax(DIMCV[(ds, sd, 0.5, 100)]))] for sd in seeds5("fig2c-condition-lds-variance")[1:]]
    print(NAME[ds], "chosen k under the four other seeds:", ks)

fig3a-eigenvalue-clusters¶

Eigenvalues of the single-condition LDSs formed distinct clusters, corresponding to rotations at about 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 and 4 Hz on every condition, along with an offset.

In [10]:
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(14, 3.2))
for ax, ds in zip(axs, DATASETS):
    lams = D[ds]["lds_lam"]
    pairs = [np.sort(np.abs(np.angle(l[l.imag > 1e-12]))) / (2 * np.pi) * 100 for l in lams]
    npair = np.array([len(p) for p in pairs])
    nreal = np.array([int(np.sum(np.abs(l.imag) <= 1e-12)) for l in lams])
    maxp = npair.max()
    med = [np.median([p[i] for p in pairs if len(p) > i]) for i in range(maxp)]
    cnt = [sum(len(p) > i for p in pairs) for i in range(maxp)]
    targets = [0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 4.0]
    ok = [abs(med[i] - targets[i]) <= 0.1 * targets[i] for i in range(min(maxp, 4))]
    print(f"{NAME[ds]}: k={D[ds]['lds_k']}; complex pairs per condition {np.bincount(npair)} ; real eigenvalues per condition "
          f"{np.bincount(nreal)} ; conditions with >=1 real: {int((nreal >= 1).sum())}/72")
    print(f"   median frequency of pair rank 1..{maxp} (Hz): {np.round(med, 2)} (conditions: {cnt}); within 10% of 0.5,1.5,2.5,4: {ok}")
    allf = np.concatenate([np.abs(np.angle(l)) / (2 * np.pi) * 100 for l in lams])
    print(f"   all eigenvalue frequencies: range {allf.min():.2f}-{allf.max():.2f} Hz; |eigenvalue| range "
          f"{min(np.abs(l).min() for l in lams):.3f}-{max(np.abs(l).max() for l in lams):.3f}")
    L_ = np.concatenate(lams)
    ax.scatter(L_.real, L_.imag, s=3)
    ax.set_title(NAME[ds]); ax.set_xlabel("real"); ax.set_ylabel("imag")
    ax.set_xlim(0.8, 1.01); ax.set_ylim(-0.25, 0.25)
    print(f"   points outside the axes: {int(np.sum((L_.real < 0.8) | (np.abs(L_.imag) > 0.25)))}")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

fig3c-eigenvalue-distance-auc¶

Eigenvalues differed between conditions only slightly more than expected from estimation noise, with ROC-AUC 0.51 to 0.58 between the between-condition distances and the noise distribution.

Distance: mean over frequency-sorted corresponding eigenvalues of their distance in the complex plane (claims); the code's vector norm is a variant. Nulls: (a) Poisson, two sets of 20 trials simulated from each condition's rates; (b) random halves of the real trials. The Methods give 500 repeats per condition; 100 are run here for each reading (deviation; time). The Poisson trials are simulated as 10 ms counts from the smoothed rates and smoothed with a 20 ms Gaussian at 10 ms resolution (deviation: the paper simulates at the resolution of its 1 ms pipeline). The rates simulated from are already smoothed and the counts are smoothed again, which lowers the noise of null (a); null (b), from the real trials, does not have this problem.

In [11]:
def eig_dist(l1, l2, how="mean"):
    a, b = ldr.sort_eigs(l1), ldr.sort_eigs(l2)
    n = min(len(a), len(b))
    if how == "mean":
        return np.mean(np.abs(a[:n] - b[:n]))
    return np.linalg.norm(a[:n] - b[:n])


def eig_null(ds, reading, nrep, sd):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    m = ds[0]
    kd = D[ds]["lds_k"]
    R, cond = D[ds]["R"], D[ds]["cond"]
    out_mean, out_norm = [], []
    if reading == "b":
        for r in range(nrep):
            a, b = ldr.split_half(cond, 72, rng, MASK[m])
            XA = ldr.cond_average(R, cond, 72, a)[..., ldr.FIT0:]
            XB = ldr.cond_average(R, cond, 72, b)[..., ldr.FIT0:]
            for c in range(72):
                la, lb = ldr.rrr_lds(XA[c], kd)[1], ldr.rrr_lds(XB[c], kd)[1]
                out_mean.append(eig_dist(la, lb)); out_norm.append(eig_dist(la, lb, "norm"))
    else:
        from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
        lam_rate = np.clip(D[ds]["X"], 0, None) * 0.01 * 20  # expected count of 20 trials per 10 ms bin
        for r in range(nrep):
            for c in range(72):
                est = []
                for _ in range(2):
                    cnt = rng.poisson(lam_rate[c]).astype(float)
                    est.append(gaussian_filter1d(cnt, 2.0, axis=1, mode="reflect")[:, ldr.FIT0:] / (0.01 * 20))
                la, lb = ldr.rrr_lds(est[0], kd)[1], ldr.rrr_lds(est[1], kd)[1]
                out_mean.append(eig_dist(la, lb)); out_norm.append(eig_dist(la, lb, "norm"))
    return np.array(out_mean), np.array(out_norm)


def eig_job(args):
    return eig_null(*args)


_jobs = [(ds, r, 100, seed("fig3c-eigenvalue-distance-auc")) for ds in DATASETS for r in ("a", "b")]
_jobs += [(ds, "b", 20, sd) for ds in DATASETS for sd in seeds5("fig3c-eigenvalue-distance-auc")[1:]]
_res = dict(zip(_jobs, ldr.pmap(eig_job, _jobs)))
EIG = {}
for ds in DATASETS:
    lams = D[ds]["lds_lam"]
    obs = np.array([eig_dist(lams[i], lams[j]) for i in range(72) for j in range(i + 1, 72)])
    obs_n = np.array([eig_dist(lams[i], lams[j], "norm") for i in range(72) for j in range(i + 1, 72)])
    EIG[ds] = dict(obs=obs, obs_n=obs_n)
    for r in ("a", "b"):
        EIG[ds][r] = _res[(ds, r, 100, seed("fig3c-eigenvalue-distance-auc"))]
    EIG[ds]["seeds"] = [_res[(ds, "b", 20, sd)][0] for sd in seeds5("fig3c-eigenvalue-distance-auc")[1:]]

suppfig2-eigenvalues-from-kinematics¶

This claim needs the reach parameters of fig6e; it is computed in the kinematics section below.

fig3g-basis-frequencies¶

The cross-validated temporal basis functions contained 3 to 4 rotations at 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 and 4 Hz, along with an offset.

In [13]:
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(14, 3))
for ax, ds in zip(axs, DATASETS):
    g, fr = D[ds]["grp"], D[ds]["freq"]
    rot_f = [fr[g == r][0] for r in range(g.max() + 1)]
    near = [min([0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 4.0], key=lambda t: abs(t - f)) for f in rot_f]
    within = [abs(f - t) <= 0.1 * t for f, t in zip(rot_f, near)]
    print(f"{NAME[ds]}: CV best k {D[ds]['k_cv']} (five seeds {D[ds]['k_seeds']}), k used {D[ds]['k']}; rotation pairs {g.max() + 1}, "
          f"real modes {(g == -1).sum()}; rotation frequencies {np.round(rot_f, 2)} Hz; nearest of 0.5/1.5/2.5/4 {near}; within 10%: {within}")
    print(f"   |eigenvalue| of the offset mode {np.abs(D[ds]['lam'][g == -1]).round(4)}")
    # the same factorization fitted on other windows (to tell a shift of frequency due to the window
    # from one in the data; verifier's request): 0 to +850 ms and -350 to +850 ms, the dataset's k
    for lab, t0 in (("0..+850 ms", int(np.searchsorted(ldr.GRID_MS, 0))), ("-350..+850 ms", 0)):
        g2, fr2 = ldr.demix(*ldr.tbf(D[ds]["X"][..., t0:], D[ds]["k"]))[3:]
        print(f"   window {lab}: rotation frequencies {np.round([fr2[g2 == r][0] for r in range(g2.max() + 1)], 2)} Hz")
    ax.plot(ldr.GRID_MS[ldr.FIT0:], D[ds]["B"].T)
    ax.set_title(NAME[ds]); ax.set_xlabel("ms from movement onset")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

tbf-shuffle-control and fig3h-recoverability¶

Shuffled data: the 1 ms bins of each trial permuted in time (one permutation for all units of a trial) before smoothing and averaging, then TBF with the dataset's k. The span permuted is the 1.5 s window read around movement onset (assumption; the paper's text does not give it). The paper's code permutes all columns of a trial's 1 ms matrix (scrambleTrials.m) and smooths and down-samples the same matrix (preprocessTrials.m), so its span is the analysis window, -350 to +850 ms; that span is run as a variant under the claim's own seed. Recoverability per condition: the variance of the basis functions explained by pinv(L(c)) X(c) (Methods, Eq. 6), on the de-mixed basis. Chance is the same measure on the shuffled data, with the shuffled basis de-mixed in the same way; the raw shuffled basis is shown as a variant.

In [15]:
def recoverability(L, B, Xw):
    out = []
    for c in range(len(L)):
        Bh = np.linalg.pinv(L[c]) @ Xw[c]
        out.append(ldr.pop_ve(B, Bh))
    return np.array(out)


SH = {}
SHW = {}
for ds in DATASETS:
    m, area = ds
    D[ds]["rec"] = recoverability(D[ds]["L"], D[ds]["B"], D[ds]["Xw"])
    SH[ds] = {}
    for sd in seeds5("tbf-shuffle-control"):
        Xs = ldr.cond_average(SESS[m]["RS"][sd][:, D[ds]["u"]], D[ds]["cond"], 72, MASK[m])[..., ldr.FIT0:]
        Bs, Ls = ldr.tbf(Xs, D[ds]["k"])
        ve = ldr.pop_ve(Xs, np.einsum("cnk,kt->cnt", Ls, Bs))
        # chance recoverability with the shuffled basis de-mixed, as the real basis is (main), and with
        # the raw SVD basis (variant)
        Bsd, Lsd = ldr.demix(Bs, Ls)[:2]
        SH[ds][sd] = dict(ve=ve, rec=recoverability(Lsd, Bsd, Xs), rec_raw=recoverability(Ls, Bs, Xs))
    # variant: shuffled over the span of the paper's code, the analysis window (scrambleTrials.m)
    for sd, RSW in SESS[m]["RSW"].items():
        Xs = ldr.cond_average(RSW[:, D[ds]["u"]], D[ds]["cond"], 72, MASK[m])[..., ldr.FIT0:]
        Bs, Ls = ldr.tbf(Xs, D[ds]["k"])
        Bsd, Lsd = ldr.demix(Bs, Ls)[:2]
        SHW[ds] = dict(ve=ldr.pop_ve(Xs, np.einsum("cnk,kt->cnt", Ls, Bs)), rec=recoverability(Lsd, Bsd, Xs))

fig3i-duration-warping¶

Reach duration per trial: movement onset to the last 1 ms sample at which hand speed is at least a tenth of its peak, within 850 ms (claims; code warpTrials.m). Per condition, the mean over its trials; correlation of |duration - mean over conditions| with recoverability, before and after warping.

In [18]:
for ds in DATASETS:
    m = ds[0]
    dur = SESS[m]["trials"]["duration_ms"]
    cdur = np.array([np.nanmean(dur[MASK[m] & (D[ds]["cond"] == c)]) for c in range(72)])
    ext = np.abs(cdur - cdur.mean())
    D[ds]["cdur"] = cdur
    r0, p0 = stats.pearsonr(ext, D[ds]["rec"])
    out = [f"{NAME[ds]}: condition duration {cdur.min():.0f}-{cdur.max():.0f} ms; unwarped rho {r0:.3f} p {p0:.3g}"]
    for key, lab in (("RW", "warped, truncated at 850 (main)"), ("RW2", "warped, post-reach to 250 ms")):
        Xwp = ldr.cond_average(SESS[m][key][:, D[ds]["u"]], D[ds]["cond"], 72, MASK[m])[..., ldr.FIT0:]
        Bw, Lw = ldr.tbf(Xwp, D[ds]["k"])
        Bw, Lw = ldr.demix(Bw, Lw)[:2]
        recw = recoverability(Lw, Bw, Xwp)
        r, p = stats.pearsonr(ext, recw)
        out.append(f"{lab}: rho {r:.3f} p {p:.3g} (recoverability mean {recw.mean():.3f})")
    print(" | ".join(out))

single-lds-variance¶

A single linear dynamical system fitted to all conditions captured on average 46 to 66% of the population variance.

In [19]:
for ds in DATASETS:
    X = D[ds]["X"]
    Xp = np.concatenate([X[c, :, ldr.FIT0:-1].T for c in range(72)])
    Xf = np.concatenate([X[c, :, ldr.FIT0 + 1:].T for c in range(72)])
    M = np.linalg.lstsq(Xp, Xf, rcond=None)[0]
    ve_a, ve_b = [], []
    for c in range(72):
        sim = np.zeros((X.shape[2], X.shape[1]))
        sim[: ldr.FIT0 + 1] = X[c, :, : ldr.FIT0 + 1].T
        for t in range(ldr.FIT0 + 1, X.shape[2]):
            sim[t] = sim[t - 1] @ M
        ve_a.append(ldr.pop_ve(X[c, :, ldr.FIT0:], sim[ldr.FIT0:].T))
        ve_b.append(ldr.pop_ve(X[c], sim.T))
    ve_a, ve_b = np.array(ve_a), np.array(ve_b)
    D[ds]["slds_ve"] = ve_a
    print(f"{NAME[ds]}: (a) -150..+850 mean {ve_a.mean():.3f} s.d. {ve_a.std():.3f} | (b) whole window, bins before -150 copied "
          f"mean {ve_b.mean():.3f} s.d. {ve_b.std():.3f} | max |eigenvalue| of M {np.abs(np.linalg.eigvals(M)).max():.4f}")

Alignment of rotations across conditions¶

Rotations are the pairs of de-mixed basis functions that share a frequency; the state space location is the column of the real (offset) mode. Noise: loadings fitted by regression on the fixed basis to two random halves of a condition's trials, 36 repeats (Methods, Measuring the across-condition alignment of rotations).

In [20]:
def comps(ds):
    g = D[ds]["grp"]
    out = [("rot%d (%.2f Hz)" % (r, D[ds]["freq"][g == r][0]), np.where(g == r)[0]) for r in range(g.max() + 1)]
    out.append(("location", np.where(g == -1)[0][:1]))
    return out


def ai_matrix(L1, B1, L2):
    """AI of each condition's activity L1[c] @ B1 onto span(L2[c']) for all c, c'. Returns (C, C)."""
    C = len(L1)
    Q = np.stack([ldr.orth(L2[c]) for c in range(C)])
    out = np.zeros((C, C))
    for c in range(C):
        Y = L1[c] @ B1
        Y = Y - Y.mean(1, keepdims=True)
        out[c] = np.sum(np.einsum("knd,nt->kdt", Q, Y) ** 2, axis=(1, 2)) / np.sum(Y ** 2)
    return out


def noise_ai(ds, nrep, sd):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    m = ds[0]
    Bp = np.linalg.pinv(D[ds]["B"])
    out = {name: [] for name, _ in comps(ds)}
    halves = []
    for r in range(nrep):
        a, b = ldr.split_half(D[ds]["cond"], 72, rng, MASK[m])
        LA = ldr.cond_average(D[ds]["R"], D[ds]["cond"], 72, a)[..., ldr.FIT0:] @ Bp
        LB = ldr.cond_average(D[ds]["R"], D[ds]["cond"], 72, b)[..., ldr.FIT0:] @ Bp
        halves.append((LA, LB))
        for name, idx in comps(ds):
            out[name].append([ldr.alignment_index(LA[c][:, idx], D[ds]["B"][idx], LB[c][:, idx]) for c in range(72)])
    return {k: np.array(v) for k, v in out.items()}, halves


AL = {}
for ds in DATASETS:
    L, B = D[ds]["L"], D[ds]["B"]
    nz, halves = noise_ai(ds, 36, seed("fig4b-plane-alignment"))
    AL[ds] = dict(noise=nz, halves=halves, obs={})
    for name, idx in comps(ds):
        AL[ds]["obs"][name] = ai_matrix(L[:, :, idx], B[idx], L[:, :, idx])
    AL[ds]["noise_seeds"] = [noise_ai(ds, 36, sd)[0] for sd in seeds5("fig4b-plane-alignment")[1:]]


def align_report(ds, name):
    O = AL[ds]["obs"][name]
    off = ~np.eye(72, dtype=bool)
    obs = O[off]
    nz = AL[ds]["noise"][name].ravel()
    A, raw = ldr.auc(nz, obs)  # raw: P(noise > observed)
    per_c_obs = np.array([O[c][off[c]].mean() for c in range(72)])
    per_c_nz = AL[ds]["noise"][name].mean(0)
    p_a = stats.wilcoxon(per_c_obs, per_c_nz).pvalue
    p_b = stats.ranksums(obs, nz).pvalue
    seeds_auc = [ldr.auc(ns[name].ravel(), obs)[0] for ns in AL[ds]["noise_seeds"]]
    return A, raw, obs, nz, p_a, p_b, per_c_obs, per_c_nz, seeds_auc

fig4c-subspace-excursion-angles¶

Across conditions, each rotation's planes spanned 6 to 20 distinct dimensions with angles above 45 degrees to each other, and more that varied above chance.

SEA to 25 dimensions, every condition tried as the seed. Excursion angles are counted after the seed plane; the count including the seed's dimensions is shown as a variant. Chance (claims: "fraction of noise SEA above the data", code singleFrequencyOverlapControl.m, not described further): SEA run on the 72 half-split estimates of a single condition's plane (36 repeats, two halves each), which differ only by estimation noise, for 24 conditions per rotation and three seed planes per run (time). A data dimension is above chance when fewer than 5% of these noise SEA curves reach its angle. This reading of the control is an assumption. The earlier threshold, the 95th percentile of the largest principal angle between two half-split planes of one condition, is shown as a variant.

In [23]:
def max_angle(Q1, Q2):
    s = np.linalg.svd(Q1.T @ Q2, compute_uv=False)
    return np.degrees(np.arccos(np.clip(s.min(), -1, 1)))


def sea_job(args):
    ds, name = args
    idx = dict(comps(ds))[name]
    planes = [ldr.orth(D[ds]["L"][c][:, idx]) for c in range(72)]
    return ldr.sea(planes, 25)


jobs = [(ds, name) for ds in DATASETS for name, _ in comps(ds)]
SEA = dict(zip(jobs, ldr.pmap(sea_job, jobs)))
# Noise SEA (claims: "fraction of noise SEA above the data", code singleFrequencyOverlapControl.m; the
# procedure is not described further, so this is an assumption): SEA run on the 72 half-split estimates
# (36 repeats x 2 halves) of one condition's plane, which differ only by estimation noise, for every
# third condition (24 per rotation), with three seed planes per run (time). A data dimension is above
# chance when fewer than 5% of these noise curves reach its angle.
def sea_noise_job(args):
    ds, name, c = args
    idx = dict(comps(ds))[name]
    planes = [ldr.orth(H[c][:, idx]) for LA, LB in AL[ds]["halves"] for H in (LA, LB)]
    return ldr.sea(planes, 25, seeds=(0, 24, 48))

rotation-orientation-dimensionality and suppfig6b-location-dimensionality¶

PCs to 80% and participation ratio from a PCA across conditions of (a) the loading columns stacked as observations, (b) the activity of the component (loading columns times basis functions). SNR dimensionality by the half-split procedure of the Methods, 100 folds: basis from partition 1, loadings regressed on it for both partitions, PCA of partition 1's loadings ("PCA on the dimensions occupied by these rotations", not mean-centred, so that the bottleneck to d PCs spans the loadings themselves); the dimensionality that maximises the alignment index between the bottlenecked partition-1 loadings and partition 2's (all dimensions searched).

In [25]:
def pca_dims(Z):
    Z = Z - Z.mean(0)
    ev = np.linalg.svd(Z, compute_uv=False) ** 2
    cum = np.cumsum(ev) / ev.sum()
    return int(np.searchsorted(cum, 0.8) + 1), ldr.participation_ratio(ev)


def snr_job(args):
    ds, sd, nfold, dmax = args
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    m = ds[0]
    names = [n for n, _ in comps(ds)]
    full_f = {n: (D[ds]["freq"][i][0] if n != "location" else 0.0) for n, i in comps(ds)}
    score = {n: np.zeros(dmax) for n in names}
    for f_ in range(nfold):
        a, b = ldr.split_half(D[ds]["cond"], 72, rng, MASK[m])
        XA = ldr.cond_average(D[ds]["R"], D[ds]["cond"], 72, a)[..., ldr.FIT0:]
        XB = ldr.cond_average(D[ds]["R"], D[ds]["cond"], 72, b)[..., ldr.FIT0:]
        B1, L1 = ldr.tbf(XA, D[ds]["k"])
        B1, L1, lam1, g1, fr1 = ldr.demix(B1, L1)
        L2 = XB @ np.linalg.pinv(B1)
        for n in names:
            if n == "location":
                idx = np.where(g1 == -1)[0][:1]
            else:
                rs = [r for r in range(g1.max() + 1)]
                if not rs:
                    continue
                r = min(rs, key=lambda r: abs(fr1[g1 == r][0] - full_f[n]))
                idx = np.where(g1 == r)[0]
            A1, A2 = L1[:, :, idx], L2[:, :, idx]
            Z = A1.transpose(0, 2, 1).reshape(-1, A1.shape[1])
            # PCs of partition 1's loadings, not mean-centred: the bottleneck below is applied to the loadings as
            # they are, so the PCs must span them (Methods, "PCA on the dimensions occupied by these rotations")
            V = np.linalg.svd(Z, full_matrices=False)[2]
            Bc = B1[idx] - B1[idx].mean(1, keepdims=True)
            G = Bc @ Bc.T
            Q2 = np.stack([ldr.orth(A2[c]) for c in range(72)])
            C1 = np.einsum("pn,cnk->cpk", V, A1)  # loadings in PC coordinates
            W2 = np.einsum("cnd,pn->cdp", Q2, V)
            # bottleneck to d PCs: A1d = V[:d].T C1[:, :d]; the AI of A1d @ Bc onto span(Q2), for all d
            Mcum = np.cumsum(np.einsum("cdp,cpk->cpdk", W2, C1), axis=1)  # (c, d, dq, k)
            Ccum = np.cumsum(np.einsum("cpk,cpl->cpkl", C1, C1), axis=1)  # (c, d, k, k)
            num = np.einsum("cpdk,kl,cpdl->cp", Mcum, G, Mcum)
            den = np.einsum("cpkl,kl->cp", Ccum, G)
            ai = (num / den).mean(0)
            score[n][: min(dmax, len(ai))] += ai[:dmax] / nfold
    return score


SNR = dict(zip(DATASETS, ldr.pmap(snr_job, [(ds, seed("rotation-orientation-dimensionality"), 100, 96) for ds in DATASETS])))
_j = [(ds, sd, 100, 96) for ds in DATASETS for sd in seeds5("rotation-orientation-dimensionality")[1:]]
_r = ldr.pmap(snr_job, _j)
SNR_SEEDS = {ds: [r for (d_, *_), r in zip(_j, _r) if d_ == ds] for ds in DATASETS}

DIMS = {}
for ds in DATASETS:
    for name, idx in comps(ds):
        A = D[ds]["L"][:, :, idx]
        za = A.transpose(0, 2, 1).reshape(-1, A.shape[1])
        zb = np.concatenate([(A[c] @ D[ds]["B"][idx]).T for c in range(72)])
        pa, pra = pca_dims(za)
        pb, prb = pca_dims(zb)
        snr = int(np.argmax(SNR[ds][name]) + 1)
        snr_s = [int(np.argmax(s[name]) + 1) for s in SNR_SEEDS[ds]]
        DIMS[(ds, name)] = dict(pc_a=pa, pr_a=pra, pc_b=pb, pr_b=prb, snr=snr, snr_seeds=snr_s)

fig5a-frequencies-segregated and suppfig6c-location-distinct-from-rotations¶

Alignment index of a component on one condition onto the same component, and onto each other component, on a different condition. Reading (a): signed-rank over the same ordered condition pairs; reading (b): the code's rank-sum test of the two distributions.

In [28]:
def cross_ai(ds, n1, n2):
    i1, i2 = dict(comps(ds))[n1], dict(comps(ds))[n2]
    L, B = D[ds]["L"], D[ds]["B"]
    return ai_matrix(L[:, :, i1], B[i1], L[:, :, i2])


def seg_report(ds, n1, n2):
    off = ~np.eye(72, dtype=bool)
    same = AL[ds]["obs"][n1][off]
    diff = cross_ai(ds, n1, n2)[off]
    return same, diff, stats.wilcoxon(same, diff).pvalue, stats.ranksums(same, diff).pvalue


def paired_direction(x, y):
    """Median and Hodges-Lehmann estimate (median of Walsh averages) of the paired differences x - y,
    and the one-sided signed-rank p that x is larger."""
    d = np.asarray(x) - np.asarray(y)
    ds = np.random.default_rng(0).choice(d, min(len(d), 3000), replace=False) if len(d) > 3000 else d  # standard subsample for speed
    w = (ds[:, None] + ds[None, :])[np.triu_indices(len(ds))] / 2
    return np.median(d), np.median(w), stats.wilcoxon(x, y, alternative="greater").pvalue

fig5c-rotations-predict-rotations and fig6b-location-predicts-rotations¶

Six folds over conditions; TBF, loadings and a ridge map fitted on 5/6 of the conditions; held-out loadings by projecting the held-out activity on the training basis (claims; code predictOneComponentFromAnother.m). Rotations in each fold are matched to the full-data rotations by frequency (assumption).

In [31]:
def fold_tbf(ds, train):
    Xtr = D[ds]["Xw"][train]
    B, L = ldr.tbf(Xtr, D[ds]["k"])
    B, L, lam, g, fr = ldr.demix(B, L)
    return B, g, fr


def match(ds, g, fr):
    out = {}
    for name, idx in comps(ds):
        if name == "location":
            out[name] = np.where(g == -1)[0][:1]
        else:
            f0 = D[ds]["freq"][idx][0]
            r = min(range(g.max() + 1), key=lambda r: abs(fr[g == r][0] - f0))
            out[name] = np.where(g == r)[0]
    return out


def svd_reduce(Xtr, frac):
    mu = Xtr.mean(0)
    U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(Xtr - mu, full_matrices=False)
    k = int(np.searchsorted(np.cumsum(S) / S.sum(), frac) + 1)
    return lambda Z: (Z - mu) @ Vt[:k].T


def predict_job(args):
    ds, sd, mode = args
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    folds = ldr.folds_of(72, 6 if mode != "loc_code" else 2, rng)
    names = [n for n, _ in comps(ds)]
    res = {}
    for te in folds:
        tr = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(72), te)
        B, g, fr = fold_tbf(ds, tr)
        mt = match(ds, g, fr)
        Bp = np.linalg.pinv(B)
        Ltr = D[ds]["Xw"][tr] @ Bp
        Lte = D[ds]["Xw"][te] @ Bp
        perm_tr, perm_te = rng.permutation(len(tr)), rng.permutation(len(te))
        if mode == "rot":
            pairs = [(a, b) for a in names[:-1] for b in names[:-1] if a != b]
            for a, b in pairs:
                Ptr = Ltr[:, :, mt[a]].reshape(len(tr), -1)
                Pte = Lte[:, :, mt[a]].reshape(len(te), -1)
                Ytr = Ltr[:, :, mt[b]].reshape(len(tr), -1)
                for null in (False, True):
                    red = svd_reduce(Ptr[perm_tr] if null else Ptr, 0.8)
                    f = ldr.ridge_fit(red(Ptr[perm_tr] if null else Ptr), Ytr, 0.1)
                    pred = f(red(Pte[perm_te] if null else Pte)).reshape(len(te), -1, 2)
                    for q, c in enumerate(te):
                        true = Lte[q][:, mt[b]] @ B[mt[b]]
                        res.setdefault((a, b, null), {})[c] = ldr.pop_ve(true, pred[q] @ B[mt[b]])
        else:
            loc = mt["location"]
            rest = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(B.shape[0]), loc)
            Ptr, Pte = Ltr[:, :, loc].reshape(len(tr), -1), Lte[:, :, loc].reshape(len(te), -1)
            Ytr = Ltr[:, :, rest].reshape(len(tr), -1)
            for null in (False, True):
                Pt = Ptr[perm_tr] if null else Ptr
                if mode == "loc":
                    f = ldr.ridge_fit(Pt, Ytr, 0.1)
                    pred = f(Pte[perm_te] if null else Pte)
                else:  # the code's variant: SVD to 90%, lambda 0.01, 2 folds
                    red = svd_reduce(Pt, 0.9)
                    f = ldr.ridge_fit(red(Pt), Ytr, 0.01)
                    pred = f(red(Pte[perm_te] if null else Pte))
                pred = pred.reshape(len(te), -1, len(rest))
                for q, c in enumerate(te):
                    Lh = np.zeros_like(Lte[q])
                    Lh[:, loc] = Lte[q][:, loc]
                    Lh[:, rest] = pred[q]
                    res.setdefault(("location", "rest", null), {})[c] = ldr.pop_ve(D[ds]["Xw"][c], Lh @ B)
    return {k: np.array([v[c] for c in range(72)]) for k, v in res.items()}


jobs = [(ds, sd, mode) for ds in DATASETS for mode in ("rot", "loc", "loc_code") for sd in seeds5("fig5c-rotations-predict-rotations")[:1]]
jobs += [(ds, sd, mode) for ds in DATASETS for mode in ("rot", "loc") for sd in seeds5("fig5c-rotations-predict-rotations")[1:]]
PRED = dict(zip(jobs, ldr.pmap(predict_job, jobs)))

fig6c-location-tracks-direction¶

PCA of the offset columns across the 72 conditions; circular correlation between target angle and the angle of each condition in the PC 1-2 plane (claims). A sign flip of PC 2 reverses the direction of travel, so both orientations are shown.

In [34]:
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(14, 3.3))
for ax, ds in zip(axs, DATASETS):
    m = ds[0]
    loc = D[ds]["L"][:, :, dict(comps(ds))["location"][0]]
    Z = loc - loc.mean(0)
    U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(Z, full_matrices=False)
    pc = Z @ Vt[:2].T
    ang = np.arctan2(pc[:, 1], pc[:, 0])
    tang = CT[m]["angle"]
    r1, p1 = ldr.circ_corr(tang, ang)
    r2, p2 = ldr.circ_corr(tang, -ang)
    print(f"{NAME[ds]}: circular correlation {r1:.3f} p {p1:.2e} | PC 2 flipped {r2:.3f} p {p2:.2e} | PC1-2 variance share "
          f"{(S[:2] ** 2).sum() / (S ** 2).sum():.3f}")
    sc = ax.scatter(pc[:, 0], pc[:, 1], c=tang, cmap="hsv", s=14, marker="o")
    ax.set_title(NAME[ds]); ax.set_xlabel("PC 1"); ax.set_ylabel("PC 2")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

jPCA¶

jPCA as in the Methods (Explaining variability in jPCA-identified rotations): activity reconstructed from the temporal basis functions (raw SVD basis over -350 to +850 ms with the dataset's k), soft-normalised (constant 5), mean-subtracted across conditions, 6 PCs, fitted on bins 20 to 40 of the grid (MATLAB indices; -160 to +40 ms). Two planes are kept for M1 and one for PMd.

In [35]:
def run_jpca(Xc_norm, conds):
    return ldr.jpca(Xc_norm[conds], np.arange(19, 40))


JP = {}
for ds in DATASETS:
    B2, L2 = ldr.tbf(D[ds]["X"], D[ds]["k"])
    Xr = np.einsum("cnk,kt->cnt", L2, B2)
    Xn, nf = ldr.soft_norm(Xr)
    Xm = Xn - Xn.mean(0)
    allc = np.arange(72)
    st = CT[ds[0]]["straight"]
    J = run_jpca(Xm, allc)
    nplanes = 2 if ds[1] == "M1" else 1
    W = [J["PC"] @ J["planes"][p] for p in range(nplanes)]
    JP[ds] = dict(J=J, W=W, Xm=Xm, nf=nf, mu_t=Xn.mean(0),
                  Jst=run_jpca(Xm, allc[st]), Jcv=run_jpca(Xm, allc[~st]))

jpca-fit-r2¶

Rotational dynamics found by jPCA fit activity within the jPCA planes with R2 of 0.64 to 0.73, higher on straight reaches (0.73 to 0.88) than on curved reaches (0.56 to 0.70).

In [36]:
for ds in DATASETS:
    J, Js, Jc = JP[ds]["J"], JP[ds]["Jst"], JP[ds]["Jcv"]
    print(f"{NAME[ds]}: (a) skew R2 all {J['R2_skew_2D']:.3f}, straight {Js['R2_skew_2D']:.3f}, curved {Jc['R2_skew_2D']:.3f} | "
          f"(b) unconstrained R2 all {J['R2_best_2D']:.3f}, straight {Js['R2_best_2D']:.3f}, curved {Jc['R2_best_2D']:.3f}")
    # per-condition R2 in the first plane of the all-condition fit; straight vs curved paired by maze
    Z = (JP[ds]["Xm"][:, :, 19:40].transpose(0, 2, 1) @ J["PC"]) @ J["planes"][0]
    Ms2 = J["planes"][0].T @ J["Mskew"] @ J["planes"][0]
    r2c = []
    for c in range(72):
        pre, d2 = Z[c, :-1], np.diff(Z[c], axis=0)
        r2c.append(1 - np.sum((d2 - pre @ Ms2) ** 2) / np.sum((d2 - d2.mean(0)) ** 2))
    r2c = np.array(r2c)
    mz = CT[ds[0]]["maze"]
    si = [i for i in range(72) if CT[ds[0]]["straight"][i] and (mz[i] + 1) in mz]
    ci = [int(np.where(mz == mz[i] + 1)[0][0]) for i in si]
    tdist = np.hypot(CT[ds[0]]["tx"][si] - CT[ds[0]]["tx"][ci], CT[ds[0]]["ty"][si] - CT[ds[0]]["ty"][ci])
    print(f"   pairing check: {len(si)} straight conditions paired with maze + 1, of which {int((~CT[ds[0]]['straight'][ci]).sum())} "
          f"curved; target distance within pairs median {np.median(tdist):.1f}, max {tdist.max():.1f} (target radius median "
          f"{np.median(np.hypot(CT[ds[0]]['tx'], CT[ds[0]]['ty'])):.1f}, file units)")
    print(f"   per-condition R2 (first plane): straight median {np.median(r2c[si]):.3f}, curved median {np.median(r2c[ci]):.3f}; "

jpca-variance-explained¶

Activity within the jPCA rotational planes explained only 7 to 12% of the population variance in peri-movement firing rates.

Per condition: the soft-normalised, mean-subtracted activity reconstructed in the retained planes, un-normalised, its summed variance over -150 to +850 ms as a fraction of the summed variance of the condition's activity (not mean-subtracted).

fig4d-jpca-variance-correlation and fig4f-plane-alignment-explains-jpca¶

The basis functions are extracted from the soft-normalised, mean-subtracted activity (-150 to +850 ms, the dataset's k), as the Methods say. Per condition: the variance of the rotational components, the variance in each retained jPCA plane, and the alignment index of the total rotational activity onto the plane.

In [39]:
J4 = {}
for ds in DATASETS:
    Xm = JP[ds]["Xm"][..., ldr.FIT0:]
    Bn, Ln = ldr.tbf(Xm, D[ds]["k"])
    Bn, Ln, lam, g, fr = ldr.demix(Bn, Ln)
    rot = np.where(g >= 0)[0]
    rv = np.array([np.var(Ln[c][:, rot] @ Bn[rot], axis=1).sum() for c in range(72)])
    J4[ds] = []
    for p, Wp in enumerate(JP[ds]["W"]):
        pv = np.array([np.var(Wp.T @ Xm[c], axis=1).sum() for c in range(72)])
        ai = np.array([ldr.alignment_index(Ln[c][:, rot], Bn[rot], Wp) for c in range(72)])
        J4[ds].append(dict(plane=p + 1, r_var=stats.pearsonr(rv, pv), r_ai=stats.pearsonr(ai, pv), npairs=int(g.max() + 1)))

Kinematics¶

Hand position every 10 ms from -350 to +850 ms, relative to the position at -350 ms, averaged per condition. Kinematic basis functions: the top two singular vectors of x and y hand velocity of all conditions of both monkeys (reading (a)), integrated to position; reading (b) fits a skew-normal and the derivative of a skew-normal to them (Methods, Extracting kinematic basis functions). Reach parameters are the least-squares coefficients of x and y position on the two position basis functions.

In [42]:
KIN = {}
vel = []
for m in ("J", "N"):
    H = SESS[m]["hand"][:, ::10]
    H = H - H[:, :1]
    Hc = ldr.cond_average(H, CT[m]["cond"], 72, MASK[m])
    KIN[m] = dict(H=H, Hc=Hc)
    vel.append(np.gradient(Hc, axis=1) / 0.01)
Bv, Bp_a, Sv = ldr.kin_basis(vel)
print("velocity singular values (top 5):", np.round(Sv[:5], 1), "share of the top two", np.round((Sv[:2] ** 2).sum() / (Sv ** 2).sum(), 3))
try:
    Bv_b, Bp_b = ldr.skewnorm_basis(ldr.GRID_MS.astype(float), Bv)
    print("skew-normal fit, correlation with the SVD velocity vectors:",
          [round(float(np.corrcoef(Bv[i], Bv_b[i])[0, 1]), 3) for i in range(2)])
except Exception as err:
    Bp_b = None
    print("skew-normal fit failed:", err)
KB = {"a": Bp_a, "b": Bp_b} if Bp_b is not None else {"a": Bp_a}
for m in ("J", "N"):
    for r, Bp in KB.items():
        P = ldr.reach_params(KIN[m]["Hc"], Bp)
        KIN[m]["P" + r] = P
        ve = np.mean([ldr.kin_ve(KIN[m]["Hc"][c], ldr.params_to_pos(P[c:c + 1], Bp)[0]) for c in range(72)])
        print(f"monkey {m}, reading ({r}): reach parameters reproduce condition-mean hand position with VE {ve:.3f}")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3))
ax[0].plot(ldr.GRID_MS, Bv.T); ax[0].set_title("velocity basis (a)")
ax[1].plot(ldr.GRID_MS, Bp_a.T); ax[1].set_title("position basis (a)")

fig6e-kinematics-predict-location¶

Ridge regression (lambda 0.1, intercept) from the four reach parameters to the offset column, 6 folds over conditions; variance explained in the offset column over held-out conditions. Kernel (a): OU, length scale 1000, no penalty; kernel (b): Gaussian, length scale 400, lambda 0.1. Shuffle: reach parameters permuted across conditions, 1000 permutations.

In [43]:
def cv_offset(P, Y, folds, model):
    pred = np.zeros_like(Y)
    for te in folds:
        tr = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(len(Y)), te)
        if model == "lin":
            f = ldr.ridge_fit(P[tr], Y[tr], 0.1)
        elif model.startswith("ou"):  # "ou": length scale 1e3 (claims); "ou_1e2", "ou_1e4": variants (scale of Bp, assumption)
            f = ldr.kernel_fit(P[tr], Y[tr], "ou", float(model[3:]) if "_" in model else 1e3, 0.0)
        else:
            f = ldr.kernel_fit(P[tr], Y[tr], "gauss", 400.0, 0.1)
        pred[te] = f(P[te])
    return 1 - np.sum((Y - pred) ** 2) / np.sum((Y - Y.mean(0)) ** 2)


def fig6e_job(args):
    ds, r, sd = args
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    P = KIN[ds[0]]["P" + r]
    Y = D[ds]["L"][:, :, dict(comps(ds))["location"][0]]
    folds = ldr.folds_of(72, 6, rng)
    out = {}
    for model in ("lin", "ou", "gauss"):
        real = cv_offset(P, Y, folds, model)
        null = np.array([cv_offset(P[rng.permutation(72)], Y, folds, model) for _ in range(1000 if sd == seed("fig6e-kinematics-predict-location") else 0)])
        out[model] = (real, null)
    for model in ("ou_1e2", "ou_1e4"):
        out[model] = (cv_offset(P, Y, folds, model), None)
    return out


_jobs = [(ds, r, sd) for ds in DATASETS for r in KB for sd in seeds5("fig6e-kinematics-predict-location")]
F6E = dict(zip(_jobs, ldr.pmap(fig6e_job, _jobs)))

suppfig2-eigenvalues-from-kinematics¶

Kinematic parameters predicted the eigenvalues poorly (mean R2 = 0.1, leave-one-out cross-validation).

Predictors: the four reach parameters, the condition's mean reach duration and a constant; targets: real and imaginary parts of each frequency-sorted eigenvalue of the single-condition LDSs; OLS, leave one condition out; R2 per component with negatives set to 0; mean over components pooled across the four datasets. Components with no variance (the imaginary part of a real eigenvalue) are left out.

In [45]:
for r in KB:
    allr2 = []
    for ds in DATASETS:
        lams = [ldr.sort_eigs(l) for l in D[ds]["lds_lam"]]
        n = min(len(l) for l in lams)
        Y = np.column_stack([np.array([l[:n] for l in lams]).real, np.array([l[:n] for l in lams]).imag])
        Y = Y[:, Y.std(0) > 1e-12]
        Xp = np.column_stack([KIN[ds[0]]["P" + r], D[ds]["cdur"], np.ones(72)])

            o = np.arange(72) != c

fig7c-ldr-encoding and suppfig7a-not-memorization¶

LDR encoding (Methods, LDR encoding; claims): 6 folds over conditions with TBF and loadings refitted on 5/6; ridge (lambda 0.1, intercept) or OU kernel regression (length scale 1000, no penalty) from the reach parameters to the vectorised loading matrix; predicted loadings times the training basis; population variance explained per held-out condition. Null: the model trained with reach parameters permuted across the training conditions, signed-rank test over conditions.

In [46]:
def encode(ds, P, folds, model, rng=None, null=False):
    ve = np.zeros(72)
    for te in folds:
        tr = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(72), te)
        B, L = ldr.tbf(D[ds]["Xw"][tr], D[ds]["k"])
        Y = L.reshape(len(tr), -1)
        Ptr = P[tr][rng.permutation(len(tr))] if null else P[tr]
        if model == "lin":
            f = ldr.ridge_fit(Ptr, Y, 0.1)
        elif model.startswith("ou"):  # "ou": length scale 1e3 (claims); "ou_1e2", "ou_1e4": variants
            f = ldr.kernel_fit(Ptr, Y, "ou", float(model[3:]) if "_" in model else 1e3, 0.0)
        else:  # nearest-neighbour regression
            f = lambda Z, Ptr=Ptr, Y=Y: Y[np.argmin(((Z[:, None] - Ptr[None]) ** 2).sum(2), 1)]
        Lh = f(P[te]).reshape(len(te), -1, B.shape[0])
        for q, c in enumerate(te):
            ve[c] = ldr.pop_ve(D[ds]["Xw"][c], Lh[q] @ B)
    return ve


def enc_job(args):
    ds, r, sd = args
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    P = KIN[ds[0]]["P" + r]
    folds = ldr.folds_of(72, 6, rng)
    out = {m: encode(ds, P, folds, m) for m in ("lin", "ou")}
    out.update({m + "_null": encode(ds, P, folds, m, rng, True) for m in ("lin", "ou")})
    ang = CT[ds[0]]["angle"]
    sext = np.floor(((ang + np.pi) % (2 * np.pi)) / (np.pi / 3)).astype(int)
    sfolds = [np.where(sext == s)[0] for s in range(6) if (sext == s).any()]
    out["sext_ou"] = encode(ds, P, sfolds, "ou")
    out["sext_nn"] = encode(ds, P, sfolds, "nn")
    if sd == seed("fig7c-ldr-encoding"):
        out.update({m: encode(ds, P, folds, m) for m in ("ou_1e2", "ou_1e4")})
        out.update({"sext_" + m: encode(ds, P, sfolds, m) for m in ("ou_1e2", "ou_1e4")})
    return out


_jobs = [(ds, r, sd) for ds in DATASETS for r in KB for sd in seeds5("fig7c-ldr-encoding")]
ENC = dict(zip(_jobs, ldr.pmap(enc_job, _jobs)))

fig7c-standard-encoding-worse¶

Standard instantaneous encoding models (Methods, Comparing the LDR encoding with standard instantaneous encoding models), 100 ms causal lag, the same 6 folds of conditions as fig7c: (1) ridge regression (lambda 0.1) on position, extent, velocity, speed, velocity angle (as its cosine and sine; assumption) and acceleration, with a baseline; (2) OU kernel regression on position, length scale 1e12; (3) OU kernel regression on velocity, length scale 1e11. The kernel penalty is not given. At these length scales the kernel matrix differs from a matrix of ones by about 1e-10, so any appreciable penalty reduces the fit to the training mean; the length scales only make sense with no penalty, as the claims give for the LDR encoder's kernel (code). No penalty (1e-8, for numerical stability) is used (assumption); the Methods' L2 of 0.1 for kernel decoders is shown as a variant.

In [49]:
def kin_features(m):
    Hc = KIN[m]["Hc"]
    v = np.gradient(Hc, axis=1) / 0.01
    a = np.gradient(v, axis=1) / 0.01
    ext = np.linalg.norm(Hc, axis=2)[..., None]
    sp = np.linalg.norm(v, axis=2)[..., None]
    ang = np.arctan2(v[..., 1], v[..., 0])
    lin = np.concatenate([Hc, ext, v, sp, np.cos(ang)[..., None], np.sin(ang)[..., None], a], axis=2)
    return dict(lin=lin, pos=Hc, vel=v)


def std_job(args):
    ds, sd = args
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    folds = ldr.folds_of(72, 6, rng)
    feats = kin_features(ds[0])
    lag = 10  # 100 ms at 10 ms bins
    tt = np.arange(ldr.FIT0, len(ldr.GRID_MS))
    out = {}
    for name in ("lin", "pos", "vel", "pos_l0.1", "vel_l0.1"):
        fname, _, pen = name.partition("_l")
        F = feats[fname][:, tt - lag]  # (c, T, f)
        mu, sdv = F.reshape(-1, F.shape[2]).mean(0), F.reshape(-1, F.shape[2]).std(0) + 1e-12
        ve = np.zeros(72)
        for te in folds:
            tr = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(72), te)
            Xtr = F[tr].reshape(-1, F.shape[2])
            Ytr = D[ds]["Xw"][tr].transpose(0, 2, 1).reshape(-1, D[ds]["Xw"].shape[1])
            if name == "lin":
                f = ldr.ridge_fit((Xtr - mu) / sdv, Ytr, 0.1)
                pr = lambda Z: f((Z - mu) / sdv)
            else:
                # penalty: none (floored at 1e-8, as the LDR encoder's kernel, whose penalty the claims give as
                # none, from the code); 0.1, the Methods' L2 for kernel decoders, is a variant
                f = ldr.kernel_fit(Xtr, Ytr, "ou", 1e12 if fname == "pos" else 1e11, float(pen) if pen else 0.0)
                pr = f
            for c in te:
                ve[c] = ldr.pop_ve(D[ds]["Xw"][c], pr(F[c]).T)
        out[name] = ve
    return out


STD = dict(zip(DATASETS, ldr.pmap(std_job, [(ds, seed("fig7c-ldr-encoding")) for ds in DATASETS])))

fig7f-ldr-decoding, trial-curvature-decoding, suppfig8-no-output-potent-dependence¶

Two folds over conditions. On the training half: TBF on trial averages (raw SVD basis, -150 to +850 ms) and a ridge map (lambda 10, intercept) from vectorised loadings to the four reach parameters. On the held-out half, single-trial loadings are 10 ms spike counts in spikes/s times the pseudo-inverse of the basis; predicted parameters times the position basis give hand position, compared with the trial's own hand position (relative to -350 ms) over -350 to +850 ms (claims; code kinFromTBFSingleTrial.m). Variance explained per trial, negatives set to 0.

In [51]:
def decode(ds, r, sd, lam=10.0, remove_potent=False, null=False):
    m = ds[0]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    Bp = KB[r]
    P = KIN[m]["P" + r]
    folds = ldr.folds_of(72, 2, rng)
    cond = D[ds]["cond"]
    C = SESS[m]["C10"][:, D[ds]["u"]][..., ldr.FIT0:]
    Xw = D[ds]["Xw"]
    if remove_potent:
        # output-potent dimensions: row space of least-squares maps from activity to hand position and velocity
        Hc = KIN[m]["Hc"][:, ldr.FIT0:]
        Vc = (np.gradient(KIN[m]["Hc"], axis=1) / 0.01)[:, ldr.FIT0:]
        Xs = Xw.transpose(0, 2, 1).reshape(-1, Xw.shape[1])
        K = np.concatenate([Hc, Vc], axis=2).reshape(-1, 4)
        Wm = np.linalg.lstsq(Xs - Xs.mean(0), K - K.mean(0), rcond=None)[0]
        Q = ldr.orth(Wm)
        Xw = Xw - np.einsum("nk,mk,cmt->cnt", Q, Q, Xw)
        C = C - np.einsum("nk,mk,cmt->cnt", Q, Q, C)
    ve = np.full(len(cond), np.nan)
    dec = np.full((len(cond), 4), np.nan)
    for te in folds:
        tr = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(72), te)
        B, L = ldr.tbf(Xw[tr], D[ds]["k"])
        Ptr = P[tr][rng.permutation(len(tr))] if null else P[tr]
        f = ldr.ridge_fit(L.reshape(len(tr), -1), Ptr, lam)
        Bpinv = np.linalg.pinv(B)
        ii = np.where(MASK[m] & np.isin(cond, te))[0]
        Lt = C[ii] @ Bpinv
        ph = f(Lt.reshape(len(ii), -1))
        pos = ldr.params_to_pos(ph, Bp)
        dec[ii] = ph
        for q, i in enumerate(ii):
            ve[i] = ldr.kin_ve(KIN[m]["H"][i], pos[q])
    return ve, dec


def dec_job(args):
    return decode(*args[:3], **args[3])


_jobs = [(ds, r, sd, {}) for ds in DATASETS for r in KB for sd in seeds5("fig7f-ldr-decoding")]

_jobs += [(ds, r, seed("suppfig8-no-output-potent-dependence"), {"lam": 1.0, "remove_potent": rp}) for ds in DATASETS for r in KB for rp in (False, True)]
DEC = {(a[0], a[1], a[2], tuple(sorted(a[3].items()))): v for a, v in zip(_jobs, ldr.pmap(dec_job, _jobs))}

for r in KB:
    for ds in DATASETS:
        m = ds[0]
        _, dec = DEC[(ds, r, s0, ())]
        ok = np.isfinite(dec[:, 0])
        cond = D[ds]["cond"]
        true = ldr.reach_params(KIN[m]["H"], KB[r])
        out = []
        for j in (2, 3):
            dres = dec[ok, j] - np.array([np.mean(dec[ok & (cond == c), j]) for c in cond[ok]])
            tres = true[ok, j] - np.array([np.mean(true[ok & (cond == c), j]) for c in cond[ok]])
            rr, pp = stats.pearsonr(dres, tres)
            out.append(f"parameter {j + 1}: rho {rr:.3f} p {pp:.1e}")
        print(f"kinematic reading ({r}) {NAME[ds]} ({int(ok.sum())} trials): " + "; ".join(out))

fig7f-decoder-beats-standard¶

Instantaneous decoders of hand position (Methods, Comparing LDR-based decoding to instantaneous decoding methods): activity 100 ms before each time point, smoothed with a 20 ms Gaussian (the single-trial rates used throughout) or a 100 ms Gaussian (10 ms counts smoothed with s.d. 10 bins, a standard approximation), in spikes/s as they are (the Methods do not standardise them); ridge regression (lambda 1) trained on single trials; OU kernel regression (length scale 100, L2 0.1) trained on a random subset of 3000 single-trial time points (the Methods' "subset of single-trial data"; the size is an assumption) or on trial averages. The same two folds of conditions as the LDR decoder. Variance explained in position per trial over -250 to +850 ms, the window the 100 ms lag allows, for both these decoders and the LDR decoder, compared by two-sided signed-rank tests. Variants: z-scored rates, and a training subset of 6000 points. As a check of each decoder, its variance explained on single trials of its training conditions is printed. The comparison is run against the LDR decoder under both kinematic readings. The GPFA decoders are not run: the paper gives neither the latent dimensionality nor the bin size, and fitting GPFA was not attempted in the time available.

from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d


def inst_job(args):
    ds, r, sd = args
    m = ds[0]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(sd)
    folds = ldr.folds_of(72, 2, rng)  # the same draw as decode() under this seed
    rng2 = np.random.default_rng(seed("fig7f-decoder-beats-standard"))
    cond = D[ds]["cond"]
    u = D[ds]["u"]
    lag = 10
    tt = np.arange(lag, len(ldr.GRID_MS))
    feats = {"20 ms": SESS[m]["R"][:, u], "100 ms": gaussian_filter1d(SESS[m]["C10"][:, u], 10, axis=2, mode="reflect")}
    H = KIN[m]["H"]
    out, insample = {}, {}
    configs = [(s, d_, z, 3000) for s in feats for d_ in ("linear, single trials", "kernel, single trials", "kernel, trial averages")
               for z in (False, True)]
    configs.append(("100 ms", "kernel, single trials", False, 6000))  # variant: a larger training subset
    for sname, dname, zs, nsub in configs:
        F = feats[sname]
        ve = np.full(len(cond), np.nan)
        ins = []
        for te in folds:
            tr = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(72), te)
            itr = np.where(MASK[m] & np.isin(cond, tr))[0]
            ite = np.where(MASK[m] & np.isin(cond, te))[0]
            if dname == "kernel, trial averages":
                Fa = ldr.cond_average(F, cond, 72, MASK[m])[tr]
                Ha = KIN[m]["Hc"][tr]
                X = Fa[:, :, tt - lag].transpose(0, 2, 1).reshape(-1, F.shape[1])
                Y = Ha[:, tt].reshape(-1, 2)
            else:
                X = F[itr][:, :, tt - lag].transpose(0, 2, 1).reshape(-1, F.shape[1])
                Y = H[itr][:, tt].reshape(-1, 2)
            # main: rates in spikes/s as they are (the Methods do not standardise); variant: z-scored
            mu, sdv = (X.mean(0), X.std(0) + 1e-9) if zs else (np.zeros(X.shape[1]), np.ones(X.shape[1]))
            X = (X - mu) / sdv
            if dname.startswith("linear"):
                f = ldr.ridge_fit(X, Y, 1.0)
            else:
                if len(X) > nsub:
                    pick = rng2.choice(len(X), nsub, replace=False)
                    X, Y = X[pick], Y[pick]
                f = ldr.kernel_fit(X, Y, "ou", 1e2, 0.1)
            for i in ite:
                Z = (F[i][:, tt - lag].T - mu) / sdv
                ve[i] = ldr.kin_ve(H[i][tt], f(Z))
            # check of the decoder: single trials of the training conditions (the trials it was trained on,
            # except for the trial-average model), 100 per fold
            for i in itr[:: max(1, len(itr) // 100)]:
                Z = (F[i][:, tt - lag].T - mu) / sdv
                ins.append(ldr.kin_ve(H[i][tt], f(Z)))
        key = (sname, dname) if (not zs and nsub == 3000) else (sname, dname + (", z-scored" if zs else f", {nsub} points"))
        out[key] = ve
        insample[key] = float(np.mean(ins))
    return out, insample


_jobs = [(ds, "a", seed("fig7f-ldr-decoding")) for ds in DATASETS]
_r = ldr.pmap(inst_job, _jobs)
INST = {ds: r_[0] for ds, r_ in zip(DATASETS, _r)}
INST_TRAIN = {ds: r_[1] for ds, r_ in zip(DATASETS, _r)}

tt = np.arange(10, len(ldr.GRID_MS))  # -250 to +850 ms, the window the instantaneous decoders can score
for kr in KB:
    nwin, ntot, nmain = 0, 0, 0
    for ds in DATASETS:
        m = ds[0]
        ldr_full, dec = DEC[(ds, kr, seed("fig7f-ldr-decoding"), ())]
        ok0 = np.isfinite(dec[:, 0])
        pos = np.full(KIN[m]["H"].shape, np.nan)
        pos[ok0] = ldr.params_to_pos(dec[ok0], KB[kr])
        ldr_ve = np.array([ldr.kin_ve(KIN[m]["H"][i][tt], pos[i][tt]) if ok0[i] else np.nan for i in range(len(ok0))])
        if kr == "a":
            print(f"{NAME[ds]}: LDR decoder over -250..+850 ms mean {np.nanmean(ldr_ve):.3f} (over -350..+850 ms {np.nanmean(ldr_full):.3f})")
        for key, ve in INST[ds].items():
            ok = np.isfinite(ve) & np.isfinite(ldr_ve)
            p = stats.wilcoxon(ldr_ve[ok], ve[ok]).pvalue
            win = (np.mean(ldr_ve[ok] - ve[ok]) > 0) and p < 0.001
            main = not key[1].endswith(("z-scored", "points"))
            nwin += win * main
            nmain += main
            if kr == "a":
                print(f"   {key[1]}, {key[0]} smoothing: mean {np.mean(ve[ok]):.3f} against LDR {np.mean(ldr_ve[ok]):.3f} "
                      f"({int(ok.sum())} trials); two-sided signed-rank p {p:.1e}; median difference {np.median(ldr_ve[ok] - ve[ok]):+.3f}; "
                      f"check on training-condition trials {INST_TRAIN[ds][key]:.3f}")
            elif not win:
                print(f"   kinematic reading (b): {NAME[ds]} {key} not beaten (p {p:.1e})")
    print(f"kinematic reading ({kr}): LDR higher with p < 0.001 in {nwin} of {nmain} comparisons with the main decoders "
          f"(raw rates, 3000 points; GPFA decoders not run)")
